takeover.status: LIVE — Takeovers Code full offer in progress
takeover.bidder: Sena & Co Limited (CEO David Sena's family trust vehicle)
takeover.offer_type: Full takeover offer, all cash, for all shares not already held
takeover.minimum_acceptance_condition: 90% of voting rights (Takeovers Code compulsory acquisition threshold)
takeover.independent_adviser_conclusion: Offer price of $0.80 assessed as FAIR
takeover.independent_directors_recommendation: Unanimous ACCEPT (Stiassny, Shaw); both intend to accept for their own holdings; independent directors were unable to negotiate Sena above $0.80
takeover.market_price_vs_offer: Current market price NZ$0.795 is trading essentially AT the $0.80 offer price, indicating the market is pricing a high probability of deal completion
takeover.implication: 2CC is now primarily a takeover-arbitrage instrument, not a going-concern DCF candidate. The DCF below is retained as the standalone / 'deal-fails' anchor value, but any DCF-implied 'upside' over $0.795 is NOT actionable while the offer is live and trading near terms — a rational holder cannot capture DCF upside independently of tendering into or being squeezed out by the offer. If the 90% compulsory-acquisition threshold is reached, remaining holders will be compelled to sell at $0.80 regardless of the DCF view.
takeover.downside_if_deal_fails: If the 90% condition is not met and the offer lapses, the stock would likely revert to an illiquid standalone level in the vicinity of the base-case DCF intrinsic value (~$0.52) or the pre-notice trading range ($0.59-$0.66), i.e. a re-rating DOWN from the current offer-anchored price is the key risk of the deal failing, not up.

inputs.lease_treatment_note: Lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. IFRS16 lease principal repayments are already deducted from owner FCF (see owner_fcf_bridge), so including lease liabilities in net debt would double-count the lease obligation. Net debt = Total Debt (borrowings only, 0.751) - Cash (3.838) = -3.087 (net cash).
inputs.sbc_source: verified NIL — no share-based payment note in FY25 or FY26 annual reports; LTI vested explicitly stated as 'nil' both years; share count flat at 45.5545m for 5+ years (no dilution, no buybacks, no options). This is a confirmed no-op, not a skipped adjustment.
inputs.sbc_value_if_noncash_memo: N/A — identical to main IV since SBC=0. There is no spread between 'SBC as real cost' and 'SBC as non-cash' treatment for this company.
inputs.units: millions except per-share and EPS figures

owner_fcf_bridge.methodology: This is an IFRS16 lease-heavy retailer. Rent is split: principal repayment sits in FINANCING activities (below OCF) and interest in finance expense. Reported/company FCF (OCF - capex) therefore OVERSTATES owner earnings by the lease principal. Owner FCF = OCF - capex - lease principal.
owner_fcf_bridge.excluded_years: FY2022 and FY2023 cash flows are excluded from FCF averaging — both are distorted by wind-down of the discontinued trade-finance/loan book (a $10.9m trade-finance repayment and large loan-receivable movements in FY2023 alone), making them non-comparable to the current retail-only cash flow profile.
owner_fcf_bridge.fy26_is_a_trough: FY2026 owner FCF of $1.513m is only 0.44x the FY24-26 median ($3.41m) and is smaller than the annual lease principal itself ($2.221m) — using FY26 as the DCF base year would understate the business materially.

method_b_fy26_normalised_for_inventory_b.note: Inventory grew 14.932 -> 18.041 in FY26, a working-capital cash use unlikely to repeat annually at this pace

method_d_structural_rou_amort_approx_equ.logic: ROU amortisation (~2.35) approx = lease principal (~2.22), so owner FCF approx = NPAT + PPE depreciation - PPE capex approx = NPAT approx = 3.2

mid_cycle_convergence.conclusion: Four independent methods converge tightly on $3.0-3.4m. Selected DCF base-year owner FCF of $3.20m sits at the center of this range and is used consistently across all three scenarios (scaled: bear 2.60, base 3.20, bull 3.90).

forward_run_rate_cross_check.usage_note: This forward run-rate supports the BULL case ($3.90 base), not the base case, which remains anchored to the mid-cycle convergence of ~$3.20m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: not_used_directly — DCF is built bottom-up from prescribed scenario growth paths off a mid-cycle owner-FCF base, not from a trailing CAGR. NPAT swung 4.8x peak-to-trough (FY22 2.594 to FY26 3.188 masks FY24 peak of 6.241 and FY23 trough of 1.292) over 5 years, making standard trailing CAGRs unreliable trend indicators for this business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Owner FCF 2yr CAGR (-39.8%) diverges sharply from Equity CAGR (+8-11%) and Revenue CAGR (+5.5%/-3.0%) — this divergence is EXPECTED and is the reason FY26 owner FCF was excluded as the DCF base year in favor of the mid-cycle convergence figure. It reflects a genuine cash-flow trough (lease principal + inventory build), not a change in underlying earnings power.
historical_growth.notes: FY2022/FY2023 revenue and FCF are not cleanly comparable to FY2024-26 due to the wind-down of a discontinued trade-finance/loan book (large one-off cash flows in FY2023). SBC is nil throughout, so there is no divergence between reported and SBC-adjusted FCF for this company — the standard SBC-growth-outpacing-cashflow check does not apply here.

premiums.rationale: Market cap ~NZ$36m, only ~6.5% genuine free float (~NZ$2.4m tradeable), just 232 shareholders on the register
Clean Car Standard cut FY26 NPAT by ~$1.7m; the carbon-credit intangible buffer was FULLY EXHAUSTED during FY26 ($1.589m -> $0.141m), leaving no cushion; a Cabinet policy review was due mid-2026
NPAT peak/trough ratio of 4.8x over five years (FY23 1.292 to FY24 6.241)
Sena & Co holds 75.9% pre-offer; minorities have no control, related-party and squeeze-out risk realised via the current takeover itself
100% NZ demand concentration plus Japan/FX procurement concentration

wacc_rationale.wacc_equals_cost_of_equity_note: Borrowings are de minimis ($0.751m against $22.15m equity), so WACC approx = cost of equity; no meaningful debt-weighting adjustment applied.
wacc_rationale.wacc_sensitivity_note: At 13% WACC, base-case IV approx $0.76; at 15%, approx $0.66; at 11%, approx $0.91. No plausible WACC assumption makes the stock look deeply undervalued at the current $0.795 price — the conclusion is robust to reasonable WACC disagreement.

sanity_check_step8c.diagnosis: No trip in either direction. The model was built on MID-CYCLE owner FCF ($3.2m) from the outset rather than on the trough (FY2026 owner FCF $1.51m = 0.44x the FY24-26 median) or the peak (FY2024 NPAT $6.24m), so the peak-extrapolation failure mode this check exists to catch could not arise. Base-case IV $0.5202 implies P/E 7.4x, P/B 1.07x and EV/EBITDA 2.55x, all BELOW the historical averages of 9.5x / 1.51x / 3.31x.
sanity_check_step8c.fix_applied: None required. Conservative assumptions were applied pre-emptively: (1) mid-cycle owner FCF base, (2) owner FCF deducts IFRS 16 lease principal (~$2.2m/yr) which reported FCF omits, (3) WACC 19.0% including +7.5pp of documented structural premiums, (4) terminal growth 1.5% reflecting structurally declining unit volumes (8,367 -> 7,239 over four years).
sanity_check_step8c.sbc_note: SBC is verified NIL for FY2024-FY2026 (no share-based payment note; LTI vested explicitly nil in FY25 and FY26; share count constant at 45,554,500). SBC-adjusted multiples are therefore IDENTICAL to reported on both sides of the comparison - no adjusted/unadjusted mixing. A small 419,230-option scheme granted Oct-2021 produced a $21k expense in FY2022, fully reversed in FY2023, and nil since. Do not 'correct' this to a non-zero figure in future runs.
sanity_check_step8c.direction_of_conclusion: The DCF finds 2CC EXPENSIVE at $0.795, not cheap: base-case IV $0.5202 is 34.6% BELOW the market price. This agrees directionally with independent adviser Simmons Corporate Finance, whose $0.71-$0.90 range brackets the $0.80 offer; the base case sits below their low end chiefly because of the 19% small-cap/illiquidity WACC applied here.
sanity_check_step8c.wacc_robustness: Conclusion is insensitive to WACC choice: IV is $0.91 at 11%, $0.76 at 13%, $0.66 at 15%, $0.58 at 17%, $0.52 at 19%. No plausible discount rate makes the stock deeply undervalued at $0.795.

ev_ebitda.note: Only FY25/FY26 have clean EBITDA + net debt data

detail.conclusion: Sanity check PASSES in neither direction — the base-case IV ($0.520) implies P/E 7.4x, P/B 1.07x and EV/EBITDA 2.55x, ALL BELOW every historical average the market has actually paid for this stock (avg P/E 9.7x, avg P/B 1.51x, avg EV/EBITDA 3.31x). This is because the model is built on a mid-cycle rather than trough or peak FCF from the outset, and the conservative outcome is driven by the 19% WACC and the low historical multiples the market has always applied to this micro-cap. The DCF says the stock is EXPENSIVE at $0.795 (current price), which agrees directionally with the independent adviser (Simmons Corporate Finance, range $0.71-$0.90), with the base case sitting below their range low end mainly because of the higher small-cap/illiquidity/regulatory WACC premiums applied here versus a professional M&A fairness opinion.

valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle_choice: Owner FCF is chosen at the mid-cycle convergence point (~$3.20m) rather than the FY26 trough ($1.513m) or any single peak year, because four independent estimation methods (historical mean/median, inventory-normalised FY26, NPAT-based reconstruction, and a structural ROU-amortisation-equals-lease-principal identity) all converge on $3.0-3.4m. Using the reported FY26 figure would understate the business; using the FY24 peak would overstate it.
valuation_philosophy.lease_adjustment: IFRS16 requires lease principal to be excluded from owner FCF because it sits in financing activities, not operating cash flow, even though it is economically a real, recurring cost of running the dealership network. Failing to deduct it (i.e. using company-reported FCF of $3.7m for FY26) overstates owner earnings by roughly 60% in FY26 alone.
valuation_philosophy.takeover_overlay: The DCF intrinsic values (Bear $0.36 / Base $0.52 / Bull $0.77 / weighted $0.54) are all standalone, going-concern estimates. They are presented as the 'what if the deal fails' anchor. They are NOT a prediction of where the stock will trade while the $0.80 Sena & Co offer remains live — the market price is currently anchored to the offer, not to standalone intrinsic value, and will likely remain within a few cents of $0.80 until the offer outcome (success/lapse) is known.

dividend_context.imputation_note: NZ gross dividends carry imputation credits; a NZ taxpayer's net CASH yield is below the headline gross figure quoted below.
dividend_context.sustainability_note: Payout-ratio policy is self-adjusting to the earnings cycle; likely superseded by the pending takeover regardless, which would end the public dividend stream via delisting if successful.

terminal_value_note: In all three scenarios the Gordon-growth perpetuity value is LOWER than the exit-multiple cap (bear: 13.87 vs cap 19.5; base: 22.68 vs cap 34.4; bull: 36.47 vs cap 57.75), so Gordon growth binds throughout — the high WACC (17-21%) applied to a modest terminal growth rate (1.0-2.0%) already produces a conservative terminal value without needing the exit-multiple cap to constrain it. The cap is retained in the model as a discipline check and would bind if WACC assumptions were lowered materially (see wacc_sensitivity_note).

entry_price.note: Entry price ($0.583) is ABOVE the base-case WACC-derived intrinsic value ($0.520). This is the expected relationship whenever WACC (19.0%) exceeds the 15% hurdle rate: discounting the same projected cash flows at a lower rate (15%) than WACC (19%) produces a higher present value, so the price that still delivers a 15% IRR sits above the WACC-derived fair value. This is a distinct case from the typical growth-company pattern (where WACC < hurdle and entry price sits modestly below IV); here the relationship inverts because 2CC's micro-cap/regulatory/cyclicality risk premium pushes WACC above the 15% hurdle itself. Practically moot regardless: both the entry price ($0.583) and intrinsic value ($0.520) sit well below the live $0.80 offer, so neither is the actionable price while the takeover is open.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (15% to 23%), Columns = terminal growth (0.5% to 2.5%). Base-case scenario FCF path and exit-multiple cap held constant; only WACC and terminal growth vary.

recommendation.summary: EVALUATE THE $0.80 CASH OFFER — do not hold for standalone DCF upside.
recommendation.detail: The standalone DCF (weighted IV $0.54, base case $0.52) does not support a value materially above the live $0.80/share Sena & Co takeover offer; if anything it suggests the offer is generous relative to a mid-cycle, appropriately-risk-adjusted standalone valuation, consistent with the independent adviser's fairness conclusion. For a minority holder, the rational action is to evaluate the cash offer on its own terms (accept, or sell on-market near the offer price) rather than to hold on a DCF-driven re-rating thesis, since: (1) the DCF does not identify meaningful standalone undervaluation at the current price: the current $0.795 price already sits close to or above every historical trading multiple the market has paid for this stock; (2) the controlling shareholder (75.9%, rising toward the 90% compulsory-acquisition threshold) limits any realistic prospect of a competing or higher bid; (3) both independent directors, informed by a professional fairness opinion, recommend acceptance. The key residual risk is if the 90% minimum acceptance condition is NOT met and the offer lapses: the stock would likely de-rate from the offer-anchored $0.795 back toward an illiquid standalone fundamental level of roughly $0.52-$0.66 (base-case DCF to pre-notice trading range), i.e. the asymmetry while the offer is live favors accepting/selling into the offer rather than speculating on either a higher bid (unlikely) or standalone re-rating (not supported by the DCF).
